brief: Goldman Sachs partner Mark Wilson argues two live market impulses support an equity upside case into year-end. AI FOMO revived this week after Meta's Muse broke out, accelerating perceived timelines to consumer AI adoption and sparking fear of missing out. Treasury yields rose again, this time on unabated US nominal growth strength shown in stronger PMI data, not AI capex funding competition or energy inflation. Equities still held gains despite that yield move. Wilson argues against two consensus views: that seven straight months of rising 10-year yields, the longest run in 50 years, risk pressuring equities lower, and that re-risking needs both Gulf de-escalation and passage past the midterms. His three counter-reasons: inflation risk fades as tariff pass-through wanes and Iran's negotiating window, open until November 2nd, could send energy prices lower, while Muse delivers a first deflationary shock to consumer goods. Growth's upside surprise fades as fiscal tailwinds diminish, so central banks will likely deliver fewer hikes than priced. Memory and some semis are over-earning, but core earnings stay strong through at least end-2027. Net: slowing growth, falling inflation, and less hawkish policy is Goldilocks, not stagflation, so Wilson would not wait for the midterms.
